title: Royal Palace, Luang Prabang

terrainReference.basis: Original public elevation at the footprint center of the main palace.

mapIdentity.provider: OpenStreetMap named palace building, distinguished from the larger museum precinct
mapIdentity.scope: OpenStreetMap’s named palace building has 16 mapped vertices. The long southeastern edge is the main frontage and fixes the orientation. The precinct and Haw Pha Bang temple have separate mapped ways.

note: The museum confirms historic Lao and French design, the reception areas, central throne hall and royal residential wing. The exact Qualla original shows the deep red roofs, white entrance and wings, central decorated gable, stairs and gold spire. Selected exterior heights and the 0.86 m model-floor offset are estimates guided by the photographed front and the untouched local terrain.
